record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Do privacy-amplification-by-iteration results known for convex optimization extend to the non-convex federated-learning setting, and can practical protocols provide formal privacy guarantees despite dynamic user eligibility, local participation decisions, and mid-protocol dropout?

evidence.quote: This “privacy ampliﬁcation via iteration” setting has been recently studied by Feldman et al. [185] for convex optimization problems. However, it is unclear whether or not the results in [185] can be carried over to the non-convex setting. ... It is therefore important to investigate and design protocols that: (1) are robust to nature’s choice (user availability and dropout), (2) are self-accounting, in that the server can compute a tight (ε,δ) guarantee using only information available via the protocol, (3) rely on local participation decision ... and (4) achieve good privacy-utility trade-offs.

artifact.status_search_result: Part 1 (extension of privacy amplification by iteration beyond the convex / non-expansive setting) has seen substantial progress: subsequent works extend the Feldman et al. (2018) analysis to noisy iterations whose gradient maps need not be non-expansive, including analyses of projected Langevin and noisy SGD with smooth (possibly non-convex) losses, and shuffled/online PNSGD variants. However, fully tight bounds matching the convex case in general non-convex federated settings are not established. Part 2 (self-accounting federated protocols robust to dynamic eligibility and dropout with tight (ε,δ) accounting) remains an active area without a single agreed-upon solution; recent work on amplification by shuffling, secure aggregation with dropout, and adaptive accounting addresses parts of the problem but does not fully resolve all four desiderata simultaneously. Overall status: partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Privacy Amplification by Iteration (Feldman et al., 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Original convex-case privacy amplification by iteration result for contractive noisy iterations.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the baseline convex-case result whose non-convex extension is the open question.

status_evidence.title: Privacy Amplification via Iteration for Shuffled and Online PNSGD
status_evidence.snippet: Extends privacy amplification by iteration analysis to shuffled and online noisy projected SGD.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions of PABI beyond the original convex setting have been obtained.

status_evidence.title: An Improved Privacy and Utility Analysis of Differentially Private SGD with Bounded Domain and Smooth Losses
status_evidence.snippet: Extends PABI to noisy iterations whose gradient map is not necessarily nonexpansive, covering smooth losses beyond convexity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work pushes PABI into non-(non-expansive) regimes relevant to non-convex federated learning.

status_evidence.title: Privacy Amplification by Iteration for ADMM with (Strongly) Convex Objective Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Further developments of amplification-by-iteration in structured optimization.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing but still convex-leaning extensions, with non-convex FL case not fully resolved.

$$ x_{k} = T_k(x_{k-1}) + Z_k, \qquad k=1,\dots,K, $$
where $Z_k\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2 I_d)$ are independent Gaussian noise vectors and only the final iterate $x_K$ is released. "Privacy amplification by iteration" refers to the phenomenon that, when each $T_k$ is a contraction (in particular, when each $f_k$ is convex and smooth and $T_k$ is a gradient step with a suitable step size), the Rényi differential privacy guarantee for $x_K$ with respect to a change in a single $f_k$ improves geometrically with the number of subsequent iterations $K-k$, even though intermediate iterates would only yield a much weaker (single-step) Gaussian-mechanism guarantee.

Part 1 (Non-convex extension). Let each $f_k:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a (possibly non-convex) $L$-smooth function with bounded-gradient sensitivity, and let $T_k$ be the corresponding noisy gradient step. Determine whether there exist quantitative privacy-amplification-by-iteration bounds for the released iterate $x_K$ analogous to those known in the convex case—i.e., bounds on the Rényi divergence between the output distributions induced by two neighboring sequences of update maps that decay (or otherwise improve) as a function of the number of iterations performed after the differing step, without requiring convexity or non-expansiveness of $T_k$.

Part 2 (Federated protocols with dynamic participation). Consider a server-coordinated iterative protocol in which, at each round $k$, an unknown subset $S_k$ of users is available, each available user independently decides locally whether to participate, and any participating user may drop out mid-round. (ii) self-accounting: the server can compute a tight $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy guarantee using only information observable during execution of the protocol;
(iii) local participation: the decision of whether to contribute in round $k$ is made by each user locally, without revealing participation to the server beyond what is necessary;
(iv) good privacy–utility trade-off comparable, up to constants, to that of an idealized protocol with fixed participation.
